data.title: EMB Mission Bound AB (publ) publishes interim report for the period January-September 2026
data.description:
During Jul–Sep 2026, the Group’s revenue mix continued to shift, with stronger technology access fees and service fees more than offsetting the decline in traditional royalty revenue. Total revenue increased by 28% compared with Jul–Sep 2025. For Jan–Sep 2026, total revenue increased by 9%, driven by growth in technology access fees and service fees, partly offset by lower royalty revenue.

At the same time, the Group’s cost base decreased across both periods. Personnel costs were lower than in the corresponding periods of 2025, which included redundancy costs arising from the Group’s restructuring program. Other operating expenses also declined, primarily due to a one-off reversal of an office restoration provision of SEK 4,937k. The operational efficiency and cost-optimisation measures implemented during 2025 continued to benefit the Jan–Sep 2026 results.

Reported EBITDA increased by 1,360% for Jul–Sep 2026 and by 189% for Jan–Sep 2026, while profit for the period increased by 385% and 843%, respectively. Excluding the one-off reversal of the office restoration provision of SEK 4,937k, EBITDA amounted to SEK 18,641k for Jul–Sep 2026 and SEK 45,046k for Jan–Sep 2026.

SIGNIFICANT EVENTS DURING THE THIRD QUARTER OF 2026

During the third quarter of 2026, the Group entered into a new lease agreement for an office in Taiwan, recognising right-of-use assets and corresponding lease liabilities of SEK 12,186k each. The new premises will replace an existing office whose lease was extended until December 2026. Under the extension agreement, the lessor waived all premises reinstatement and restoration obligations, resulting in the reversal of an office restoration provision of SEK 4,937k.

SIGNIFICANT EVENTS AFTER THE END OF THE PERIOD

On 21 October 2026, EMB Mission Bound AB (publ) entered into an agreement to acquire 51% of Cyprus-based Cleverpath Holdings Limited (“MegaBet Plus”) from Dennis Ang. Completion is subject to approval from the Cyprus National Betting Authority and is expected during the first quarter of 2027. The preliminary consideration of EUR 4.1 million (approximately MSEK 45.6), subject to customary adjustments, comprises EUR 3.0 million for the equity interest and EUR 1.1 million for rights to the Class A and Class B NBA bonds. Settlement will be through a promissory note to be set off against newly issued Company shares, at a subscription price corresponding to the volume-weighted average price of the Company’s shares over the 30-day period immediately preceding the closing date. The seller also holds a put option requiring the Company to acquire a further 39% for EUR 2,668,422, exercisable 12–15 months after completion. Settlement may be in cash, Company shares or both, subject to the Company’s legal and regulatory capacity. In connection with the transaction, the Company advanced an initial EUR 150,000 under the loan agreement to MegaBet Plus. The loan agreement allowed a further advance of EUR 150,000 at MegaBet Plus’s request and subject to the Company’s approval. The Company subsequently advanced the second tranche, bringing the total amount advanced under the loan agreement to EUR 300,000. The loan matures on 21 April 2027 and may be extended by the Company.

A WORD FROM THE CEO

Dear Shareholders,

The third quarter of 2026 marks a further step forward in the strategic transition we began in 2025. In Q1, we reported early evidence that our operational changes and focus on technology partnerships were improving performance. In Q2, growth in technology access and service fees offset the decline in traditional royalty revenue. Q3 builds on that progress, with these activities now driving overall revenue growth and further improving profitability.

Revenue for the quarter reached SEK 51.7 million, up 28% from the corresponding period last year and 11% from Q2. This follows quarterly revenue of SEK 38.6 million in Q1 and SEK 46.4 million in Q2, demonstrating the commercial progress made during the year. Revenue for the first nine months rose 9% to SEK 136.6 million, following a broadly unchanged first half.

The changing composition of our revenue remains central to this development. Technology access fees increased by 132% year on year to SEK 15.3 million in Q3, while service fees grew by 69% to SEK 32.6 million. Together, these activities accounted for about 93% of quarterly revenue, more than offsetting the continued decline in royalties. Growth reflected a new customer gaining access to selected components of our proprietary technology, along with new service engagements and expanded scope of work with existing customers.

These results support the direction described in our previous reports: developing EMB Mission Bound as a technology partner with deeper involvement in customers’ platforms and operations. Our focus remains on converting initial engagements into lasting relationships across technology development, integration, maintenance and support. We recognise technology access fees when we grant access, so their timing can influence quarterly performance; continued growth in our service business remains an important part of building a more resilient revenue base.

Reported EBITDA reached SEK 23.6 million, up from SEK 14.5 million in Q2, while profit increased to SEK 15.1 million from SEK 7.3 million. Profit for the first nine months amounted to SEK 27.5 million, compared with a loss of SEK 3.7 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

These results include a one-off benefit of SEK 4.9 million from the reversal of an office restoration provision following the landlord’s waiver of the related obligations. The year-on-year cost comparison also benefits from the absence of restructuring charges incurred in 2025. While our earlier efficiency measures continue to support performance, underlying personnel costs have increased as we expand our team. Maintaining discipline as we invest in the capacity to serve customers remains essential.

Our financial position strengthened further, with cash of SEK 24.0 million and net assets of SEK 73.7 million at the end of September. Operating cash flow for the first nine months increased by 38% to SEK 35.9 million. However, quarterly operating cash flow of SEK 7.5 million was below both Q2 and the corresponding quarter last year, reflecting working-capital outflows, particularly increased receivables.

After the reporting period, we entered into an agreement to acquire a 51% stake in Cyprus-based Cleverpath Holdings Limited, known as MegaBet Plus. The transaction has preliminary consideration of EUR 4.1 million, to be settled through the issue of EMB shares as described in this report. Completion remains subject to approval from the Cyprus National Betting Authority and is expected in the first quarter of 2027. This is a significant development for the Group, and careful execution and capital discipline will be essential as the transaction progresses.

Looking ahead, our priorities remain consistent with those set out earlier this year: commercialising our proprietary technology, expanding our customer base and deepening relationships with existing partners. We will continue to develop our platform and AI-enabled capabilities while maintaining close attention to costs, working capital and the quality of earnings. Progress across the first three quarters gives us greater confidence in our direction and reinforces the importance of disciplined execution.

On behalf of the Board and leadership team, I would like to thank our employees, partners and shareholders for their continued commitment and support.

Stockholm, 20 November 2026

Chi Ho Li

CEO

data.title: Equinor Fends Off Cyberattack Detected Earlier This Week
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Equinor said Friday that it had stopped a dayslong cyberattack that had targeted some of its systems.

The Norwegian energy company detected the attack on Tuesday but said it wasn't a virus attack, so there was no chance of it spreading, and that it also didn't appear to be specifically targeting Equinor.

Production has been running as normal throughout, and there are no signs that data has been stolen or altered, it said.

"There is also no indication that the attack has had any negative consequences for employees, partners or suppliers," the company said.

Equinor has been in talks with national security authorities, and the incident has been reported to police.

Write to Dominic Chopping at dominic.chopping@wsj.com

data.title: Dan Niles Says Anthropic Is More Likely To Survive The ‘Agentic AI Commoditization’ Than OpenAI — ‘Price Competition Is Increasing’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Niles welcomed Anthropic’s 17% IPO gain but doubted whether the stock can stay above $83. 
  • Niles sees Anthropic as a long-term AI survivor but warns of slowing growth and rising price competition. 
  • Niles said OpenAI and Anthropic’s combined quarterly revenue growth slowed to 50% in Q3 from 75% in Q2. 

Anthropic’s (ANT) blockbuster market debut impressed on paper, but Dan Niles of Niles Investment Management says the harder test lies ahead. The portfolio manager argues Anthropic is more likely than OpenAI to survive the commoditization of agentic AI, even as price competition squeezes margins and the stock faces a 30-day green shoe test.

Anthropic stock slumped 5% in Friday’s premarket after a 17% rally during its Nasdaq debut on Thursday.

Anthropic IPO Raises More Than Expected

In his latest X post, Niles said Anthropic’s IPO did what it needed to do. The company upsized both the share count and the price, raising more than it first planned, and the stock closed 17% higher at the end of day one. That clears the 10% to 15% bar Niles uses to call an offering of this size a success.

However, Niles said shares opened 34% higher, touched +39% within minutes, then bled into the close. Niles says a healthy debut closes above its open. This one didn’t, which suggests buyers shut out of the allocation were hungrier than holders finally able to cash in.

“The real test of whether this was a successful IPO will come over the next 30 days during the green shoe window. Does the stock stays above its $83 IPO price in a tough tape for AI related stocks? I am not so sure.”

Niles Sees Anthropic As A Long-Term Survivor Than OpenAI

Niles’ long-term case for Anthropic has support. He said Anthropic courted paying enterprises from day one while OpenAI chased consumers used to free services. “There is scarcity value in Anthropic being the first pureplay LLM that investors have and it is likely to be fast tracked into the indices,” said Niles.

Listing the negatives, Niles said, combined revenue growth for OpenAI and Anthropic slowed from roughly 75% quarter-on-quarter in Q2 to about 50% in Q3. OpenAI’s price cuts lifted its growth from about 17% to 50% but dragged Anthropic’s from 144% to 47%. Anthropic’s adjusted operating margin slipped from 19% to 15%, while OpenAI’s losses widened from about $10.1 billion to $10.9 billion.

“Price competition is increasing, rev growth is slowing and operating margins are dropping for the two leading LLMs while capital commitments are massive. But the opportunity is massive as well and Agentic AI is in its nascency.’

“If I had to pick one LLM that survives the commoditization of this layer, Anthropic would be it. But it is not a favorite of mine for AI overall in the near-term.”

ANT Stock: Retail View 

Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. The stock recorded a 748% surge in message volume over the past 24 hours.

data.title: Cambodia exploring tokenised bonds to cut borrowing costs, cbank governor says
data.description:
Cambodia's central bank is exploring the tokenisation of government bonds as a way of lowering the nation's cost of borrowing, which has been driven up by the country's reliance on the US dollar, the bank's governor said on Friday.

  • National Bank of Cambodia governor Chea Serey told Reuters on Friday that the central bank is exploring the tokenisation of government bonds with Japan's SBI Holdings

  • Bond tokenisation could make it possible for Cambodia's diaspora to invest smaller amounts of money back into the nation

  • "If they know that the money is going to be (invested) in a bridge or a hospital, then it's okay for them to receive 1% or even no interest at all because they know, as long as they can get their principal back," she said at a Singapore Fintech Festival panel on Friday

  • "This will then help Cambodian government to raise much cheaper funds and for more meaningful purposes," she added

  • Because 90% of the economy adopts the US dollar and its corresponding interest rate, the high cost of funding has also weighed on the economy, she said

  • Serey said that Cambodia faces headwinds in the form of higher energy costs, which have contributed to a rising inflation rate, which stood at 5.3% in September

  • In September, the IMF projected that Cambodia's economic growth would slow to 3% in 2026 amid "higher energy costs, weaker tourism and remittances, slowing garment exports, subdued domestic demand, and tighter financial conditions".

  • Serey said she is optimistic that the country will outperform the projection, given an expected pick-up in tourism arrivals towards the year-end peak season

data.title: ‘Dean Of Valuation’ Says Nvidia Is 30% Below Fair Value, Waits For $140 — Calls Jensen Huang ‘Great CEO, But Human’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Damodaran said he would buy NVDA if it drops below $140.
  • Nvidia’s market capitalization has shrunk by more than $2 trillion to $3.52 trillion since Haung first admitted to an affair at the start of last week. 
  • Apple CEO Tim Cook “is not a good fit for Nvidia today,” he said. 

Valuation expert and New York University professor Aswath Damodaran called Jensen Huang a “great CEO” and said he would buy Nvidia (NVDA) stock if it drops below $140, while also offering a view on the various successor candidates discussed.

"For me, that value is about 30% below my estimated value of $4.8 trillion, yielding a breakeven value per share of around $140 per share, and I have a limit buy waiting at that price,” Damodaran said in a new blog post.

“If it happens, I will have Nvidia back in my portfolio, and if it does not, there are other stocks to buy!"

NVDA Fallout

Nvidia’s market capitalization has shrunk by more than $2 trillion to $3.52 trillion since Huang first admitted to an affair at the start of last week. Nvidia announced his resignation last Thursday and appointed CFO Colette Kress as the interim chief.

The shakeup has affected the broader AI industry, given that Huang was central to billions of dollars in financing and partnerships with dozens of key AI firms. Nvidia, which is looking for a new CEO, is not out of the woods yet. On Thursday, California launched a probe into whether Nvidia helped China secure advanced AI technology and misled shareholders.

Damodaran cautioned that the stock slide does not automatically make it cheap, saying that “Nvidia’s intrinsic value itself has likely dropped due to leadership loss and scandal fallout.”

China ‘Wild Card’

“The wild card in this story is the China twist,” Damodaran wrote. If allegations about official Chinese government ties and chip sales through Asian business fronts prove true, the legal and regulatory consequences could persist regardless of who leads Nvidia, he said.

If the disruption from Huang’s departure is strictly short-term, such as transition delays, margin pressure, or near-term legal friction, the damage to Nvidia's equity value is contained to a 5% to 10% drop in most scenarios, he said.

However, if Nvidia pulls back on its aggressive customer financing and ecosystem marketing, long-term revenue growth and margins could erode much more severely.

NVDA CEO Search

Damodaran said CEO Kress and other insiders are promising candidates, but said Apple CEO Tim Cook “is not a good fit for Nvidia today” unless appointed temporarily to manage a crisis.

"Jensen Huang has been a great CEO, but last week was a reminder that he is human… The essence of corporate governance is that even the very best managers need restraints to prevent overreach, and that giving them complete power in perpetuity is a recipe for regret," he wrote.

NVDA stock is now down 40% from its early-October peak and 21% year to date. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for NVDA dipped on Friday but remained in the ‘extremely bullish’ zone.

data.title: Asian Shares Tumble As Tech Selloff Deepens
data.description:
BEIJING (dpa-AFX) - Asian stocks plummeted on Friday as Anthropic's record listing in New York failed to stem concerns over slower AI infrastructure spending and rising debt loads in the sector.

After the release of hawkish Federal Reserve's October policy meeting minutes, investors are also recalibrating their expectations pertaining to upcoming rate decisions.

Speaking at an event on Thursday, Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said stronger economic growth and a labor market at full employment meant inflation should remain the priority for monetary policymakers.

Ahead of the Fed's December meeting, she favored a gradual approach to rate increases, giving the economy time to adjust to higher short-term borrowing costs.

Financial markets have fully priced in a 25-basis point hike at the Fed's December meeting, with a small chance of a super-sized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

The next PCE inflation report is scheduled for release on November 25, with analysts expecting the report to show annual core inflation at 3.2 percent, well above the Fed's 2 percent target.

The U.S. dollar index held near a 19-month high in Asian trading and headed for a fourth weekly gain as AI jitters fueled safe-haven demand.

U.S. Treasury yields dipped to hover near a one-week low on safe-haven bids as investors reassessed equity and AI-related risks.

Gold prices fell more than 2 percent to $3,550 an ounce and headed for their biggest weekly decline since March as hawkish Fed remarks signaled more interest-rate hikes in the coming months.

Brent crude futures edged up toward $93 a barrel but remained on track for a third consecutive weekly decline on signs of abundant global supply.

China's Shanghai Composite index fell 1.22 percent to 3,533.79 as the AI trade cooled and new U.S. licensing rules for advanced chips targeting markets such as Singapore took effect.

Earlier today, China's central bank kept its one-year loan prime rate at 3.0 percent and five-year at 3.5 percent for an 18th straight month, as widely expected.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng index slumped 1.89 percent to 22,410.80, approaching bear-market territory on concerns over China's economy and tighter U.S. restrictions on chip exports. Tencent Holdings dropped 1.3 percent after reporting a slowdown in quarterly revenue growth.

Japanese markets closed at a seven-month low due to a deepening selloff in artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks reliant on global supply chains.

Additionally, data showed Japan's consumer price inflation grew to a 11-month high in October on a sharp increase in food prices, boosting the odds for a BoJ rate hike next month.

The Nikkei average slumped 5.06 percent to 56,436.65 while the broader Topix index tumbled 3.88 percent to 3,674.22. SoftBank nosedived 14.5 percent and Kioxia Holdings plummeted 11.7 percent.

Seoul stocks hit a 10-month low on concerns over the sustainability of the AI investment boom. Investors ignored data that showed South Korea's producer prices declined for the first time in three months in October.

The Kospi index fell 5.21 percent to 4,869.96 on continued foreign selling. Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and SK Square plunged 6-8 percent on mounting concerns over AI infrastructure investment returns and rising financing costs.

Overnight, U.S. stocks fluctuated before ending deep in the red as concerns over AI infrastructure spending, semiconductor valuations and the outlook for interest rates overshadowed investor enthusiasm over Anthropic PBC's solid market debut.

Reports warning of risks from chipmaker AMD's ties with Chinese entities and Walmart's disappointing annual sales forecast also weighed on sentiment.

In economic news, labor market data showed first-time claims for unemployment benefits unexpectedly increased slightly last week.

The S&P 500 fell 2 percent to extend losses for a sixth day running and hit a six-month closing low.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plunged 2.3 percent to reach its lowest closing level in seven months while the narrower Dow plummeted 2.2 percent to a six-month low.

data.title: Signal restricts screenshots to block AI agents from reading messages
data.description:
Key points:
  • Signal warns of 'existential threat' to its privacy guarantee from AI agents on devices
  • Company urges tech giants to provide ways to stop AI accessing sensitive data

By Katie Paul

Encrypted messaging service Signal said on Friday it would restrict screenshots to stop AI agents from reading private chats on phones, warning that the tech industry's push to embed AI in consumer devices was eroding its ability to guarantee privacy.

Signal, widely regarded by privacy advocates as a leader in secure messaging, called its new protections "incomplete" and urged operating system providers Apple , Alphabet's Google and Microsoft to give app developers more concrete ways to block the agents from accessing sensitive data.

It also called on those companies to provide more information about how their agents function, so developers can assess what data the bots are accessing and adjust their systems accordingly.

The move reflects growing tension between privacy-focused apps and the biggest tech companies, which are racing to roll out AI agents designed to see what is on a user's screen and take actions based on it.

Signal identified as particularly worrisome the AI capabilities built directly into operating systems, like Apple's Siri AI and Google's Gemini Intelligence, because of how deeply they are integrated into people's devices.

Operating systems maintain the environment in which Signal and other applications must exist, the company said.

"Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy. This is an existential threat to Signal, and our ability to responsibly uphold our mission," it said in a blog post provided to Reuters ahead of its release on Signal's website.

To prevent agents from scanning Signal messages, the service is introducing new settings blocking screenshot access on people's phones and switching those restrictions on by default. Users will receive pop-up windows giving them options to disable the blocks when Signal detects screenshot attempts or efforts by an AI assistant to access the screen, depending on the device.

Signal similarly blocked Microsoft's Recall AI from taking screenshots on Windows last year. It said it was unable to reliably offer such protections on Apple's macOS.

GETTING AROUND PROTECTIONS

Agents that can take actions on behalf of users are billed as the next big wave of AI technology, capable of surfacing relevant information from across different apps and executing time-saving tasks like answering emails, booking appointments and making online purchases autonomously, without direct instructions.

However, that reach can get around the protections that apps like Signal build for themselves.

Reuters reported earlier this week that Meta's Muse agent was able to bypass its own official "Connector" tool to access Signal messages on both an Apple computer and a phone using Google's Android system. In both cases, Muse used broad operating system-level permissions granted during the app's initial setup to pull in the messages, using those authorizations in ways a user might not anticipate.

On Apple's macOS, for instance, it used a combination of the computer’s accessibility and screenshot tools, repurposing settings Apple offers for people with disabilities to navigate over to Signal, take screenshots of chats there, extract text from those pictures and reproduce the messages inside the Muse app.

An operating system update from Apple this week effectively closed that specific pathway, but also introduced a new set of permissions aimed at agents that offers similar capabilities paired with additional user warnings.

Meta said in response to Reuters' reporting that agents need to see and interact with people’s computers in order to work on their behalf, and that Muse can access other apps only via permissions users explicitly grant.

Signal said that developers should have straightforward ways of opting their apps out of such data processing by AI assistants entirely, specifically mentioning screen reading, notifications and other file system access.

The service, owned by a non-profit foundation, promises its users a secure messaging experience by limiting the data it stores on its own servers, eschewing ads and offering end-to-end encryption, meaning it cannot access and read the conversations conducted on its app.

AI systems that scan people's screens can undermine those protections by pulling the messages out of Signal's secure environment and into whatever other servers the agent is using, it said in the post.

data.title: PRESS RELEASE: Qflow welcomes Mätspecialisten and strengthens its offering in surveying
data.description:
Qflow welcomes Mätspecialisten i Ale AB as part of Qflow Group. Mätspecialisten is a specialised surveying consultancy in Gothenburg with strong expertise in surveying and production support for building and civil engineering projects. The company will become part of the group company MEXL, thereby strengthening MEXL’s offering in surveying. The acquisition broadens the group’s surveying expertise and creates a strong foundation for continued growth in western Sweden.

We are delighted to welcome Mätspecialisten to Qflow. Henrik, Stefan and Marcus have built a highly skilled team with a strong reputation in western Sweden – reflected not least in the fact that virtually all of their customers come back. Mätspecialisten is an excellent fit for the group and complements our existing surveying expertise. Together, we can offer our customers specialist surveying expertise throughout the entire project lifecycle, from design to production, while giving the team better conditions to keep growing.

— Emile Hamon, COO, Qflow Group

Mätspecialisten is a surveying consultancy with offices in Gothenburg. Its services include excavation surveying, setting out of foundations, walls and installations, machine control, earthworks management, design and project management, and the company works with modern surveying technology. Its assignments mainly involve civil engineering projects and larger building projects such as housing, schools, swimming facilities and industrial premises. Its customers are primarily building and groundwork contractors, and the vast majority of assignments come from returning customers.

For a long time, Mätspecialisten has had more assignments than we could take on. We wanted to grow, but administration held us back. When we came into contact with MEXL, which aims to become Sweden’s best employer, we immediately understood that this was the path we should take. We reached out to Qflow, which also saw the value for all parties: Mätspecialisten, MEXL and Qflow. The collaboration was under way even before the agreement was finalised, and now that we have signed, further collaborations are getting started. We look forward to what lies ahead!

— Henrik Brycke, CEO, Mätspecialisten

About Qflow

Qflow Group brings together the best consultants in the built environment sector, and together we are creating a smarter and more sustainable society — through innovation and collaboration for the future.

Today, Qflow comprises 42 companies within the group, with approximately 1,350 consultants and a turnover of approximately SEK 2,500 million. Qflow is a leading player in the built environment consulting market and brings together leading specialists in the sector.

Our network includes some of the best consultants, creating better flow in the construction and infrastructure sector. We do this through smarter project management and technical solutions. Together, Qflow Group helps connect a fragmented value chain and identify synergies between contractors that can foster innovation and development.

data.title: Juniper Green brings live 109 MWp of solar, 95 MWh of BESS in India
data.description:
November 20 (Renewables Now) - Indian independent renewable energy power producer (IPP) Juniper Green Energy (544853:BOM) has expanded its operational portfolio with the commissioning of a 109-MWp solar plant in Maharashtra and a 95-MWh battery in Rajasthan.

The company, which completed its INR-18-billion (USD-193.9m/EUR 176.7m) initial public offering this summer, said on Friday that it now has roughly 2.95 GWp of renewables energy assets in its installed fleet, as well as 698 MWh of battery energy storage systems (BESS).

In Maharashtra, Juniper Green has brought online the photovoltaic (PV) component of its solar-wind hybrid project in the town of Tuljapur in Dharashiv district. The solar plant is connected to a 132-kV substation and will be operated under a 25-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL).

Meanwhile in Rajasthan, the company has hooked to the Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) an additional 95 MWh of BESS capacity at its integrated renewable energy and storage facility in Barmer.

“As we continue to scale our operations, our focus remains on building a resilient energy platform that can deliver reliable, sustainable power and contribute meaningfully to India’s clean energy ambitions,” said CEO Ankush Malik. He noted that the new additions to Juniper Green’s portfolio are aligned with the company’s commitment to applying a more integrated approach that combines renewable generation with storage and flexibility.

Juniper Green’s total portfolio of operational, under-construction, contracted and awarded projects includes over 11 GW of generation and 8.9 GWh of BESS capacity.

(INR 10 = USD 0.0108/EUR 0.098)
